members.title: Datacentres to create 70% more carbon emissions by 2030, IEA report warns
members.lead: Global energy watchdog forecasts huge rise as US and China turn to fossil fuels to power AI growth agendas The world’s datacentres will create 70% more carbon emissions within the next four years as the US and China turn to fossil fuels to power their AI growth agendas, according to the world’s energy watchdog. The International Energy Agency (IEA) warned that datacentres will consume twice as much electricity by 2030 compared with today, with the global expansion of artificial intelligence accounting for three-quarters of this growth. members.title: US, China can help end Ukraine war, Trump tells Xi before trilateral with Putin
members.lead: Trump says US, China can help end war in Ukraine Trump calls Putin a “friend” Trump meets Xi, Putin separately before unprecedented trilateral Analysts say gathering is unlikely to produce major agreements . US President Donald Trump told his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping on Thursday that they should both help end the war in Ukraine ahead of their unprecedented three-way meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin. The diplomatic gathering of the leaders of the world’s largest nuclear powers is unlikely to produce major agreements, analysts say, given deep differences over Ukraine, Iran, nuclear weapons and trade. But it has unnerved smaller countries that fear their interests might be disregarded. Trump met Putin and Xi separately ahead of the trilateral talks, calling the Russian leader a “friend”. The Kremlin said they discussed Ukraine and that Putin left the meeting in an “excellent” mood. When meeting Xi right after, Trump thanked him for a lavish welcome and expressed hope that their trilateral with Putin would be successful. . “We’re looking to both help with respect to the war with Russia and Ukraine,” Trump said. “I’d like to see it ended.” Trump said both presidents felt strongly about oil having to flow through the Strait of Hormuz, which has been disrupted by the Iran war. Xi did not mention Ukraine or Iran in his remarks. Patricia Kim, foreign policy fellow at the Brookings Institution, said China would not want to be seen as brokering a deal over Ukraine, given the “problematic optics” of Kyiv and European leaders not taking part. . “Xi has characterized the Russia-Ukraine war as fundamentally a European problem, making Beijing even less inclined to assume responsibility for resolving it,” Kim said. . members.title: Trump, Xi, Putin issue 'peace declaration' after summit
members.lead: China, the United States and Russia issued a "peace declaration" on Thursday following an unprecedented summit of their leaders in the Chinese city of Shenzhen. The joint statement was initially published by Chinese state media and the Kremlin, with nothing released by the White House so far. It said presidents Xi Jinping, Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump had "engaged in an in-depth exchange of views on the current international situation and committed themselves to upholding strategic stability and international security". The countries "plan to increase the production and supply of refined petroleum products", it added, reaffirming "the importance of the stable flow of energy". They would also "engage in dialogue on reducing nuclear risks and preventing nuclear proliferation", it said. . The statement took aim at the International Criminal Court, saying that it and similar institutions "must not abuse their jurisdiction". The leaders also "acknowledged the vital importance of the principle of state consent and the respect for (diplomatic) immunity enjoyed by state officials", and said each country was "committed" to advancing the reform of the United Nations. In remarks carried by state news agency Xinhua, Xi described the meeting as "positive, constructive, and fruitful". "The three countries share a common perspective on safeguarding world peace," the Chinese leader said, adding: "The seeds sown during today's trilateral meeting will undoubtedly take root, sprout, and bear fruit." Trump departed Shenzhen shortly after the summit's conclusion.

members.title: First Thing: Trump, Xi and Putin hold historic trilateral meeting in China
members.lead: The three leaders spoke about international peace and nuclear weapons as Trump called Putin a ‘friend’. Plus, yes, GTA VI is really finally here, and the critics have their verdict: masterpiece Don’t already get First Thing in your inbox? Sign up here Good morning. Donald Trump has met Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping at the Apec summit in Shenzhen, and said the three leaders were “really making history”. The trilateral meeting lasted roughly an hour and a half, according to Chinese state media. On arrival the US president described his Russian counterpart as “my friend”. Putin told Xi and Trump that their countries shared “many converging interests” when it came to resolving conflicts, including the full-scale war in Ukraine, which the Russian president started in 2022. What was unusual about China’s welcome to the Japanese delegation? Apec’s Chinese hosts went out of their way to give world leaders a warm welcome as they arrived in Shenzhen, with one exception. Japan’s prime minister, Sanae Takaichi, had to make do with a modest guard of honour and a welcome from a relatively junior Chinese government official. The Guardian is live blogging the Apec summit.
